content.intro: M5: Energy Governance for a Just Energy Transition

content.text: This lesson introduces the foundations of energy governance and its central role in shaping a just energy transition. It highlights the key governance principles, and examines how weak governance, fossil fuel lock-ins, and regulatory capture can undermine progress. Discussing the actors in energy governance, the chapter emphasizes that energy transitions succeed not just through technology or investment, but through strong, <ai prompt="Explain participatory governance.">participatory governance 💬️</ai> systems that engage all levels of society and ensure fair, transparent, and adaptive decision-making.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Introduction to Energy Governance
lessons.description: This lesson introduces energy governance as a critical foundation for achieving just and sustainable energy transitions. It highlights how effective, inclusive, and accountable governance systems are essential to overcome challenges like fossil fuel lock-in, market failures, and energy inequality, ensuring that the benefits of the transition are equitably shared and aligned with long-term climate goals.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Actors in Sustainable Energy Governance
lessons.description: The transition to sustainable energy systems represents one of the most pressing and complex challenges of the 21st century. Addressing this multifaceted imperative effectively demands a paradigm shift from traditional, siloed governance models to a comprehensive Whole-of-Society Approach (WSA)his lesson provides an examination of the WSA in sustainable energy governance, defining its core principles, identifying key stakeholders, and elucidating the profound benefits it offers.
